questions.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+2}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{2} & 1 & 2 \\  & ↓ & \frac{3}{2} \\  & 1 & \frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{7}{2})}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int (1+\frac{7}{2x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\int \text{d}x+7\int \frac{1}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[x+\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{7}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9x-2}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9x-2}{4(x+1/4)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9x-2}{(x+1/4)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{4}$ | $9$ | $-2$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{9}{4}$ |
|  | $9$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9x-2}{(x+1/4)} & =9-\frac{(17/4)}{(x+1/4)} \\  & =9-\frac{17}{4x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9x-2}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}(9-\frac{17}{4x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[9{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x-17{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[9x-\frac{17}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[9(1-0)-\frac{17}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|5|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[9-\frac{17\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{4}] \\  & =\frac{9}{4}-\frac{17}{16}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$
